function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, but you can easily check your own download/upload speeds yourself. Here are a few quick options: | Method | How to do it | What you’ll see | |--------|--------------|-----------------| | **Web‑based speed test** | Visit a site like or and click “Go” (or “Start”). | Download speed, upload speed, and ping. | | **Command‑line (speedtest‑cli)** | 1. Install the tool:
`pip install speedtest-cli`
2. Run it:
`speedtest` | Download/Upload speeds in Mbps, ping, and server info. | | **Windows PowerShell** | `Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://raw.githubusercontent.com/speedtest-net/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py -OutFile speedtest.py; python speedtest.py` | Same as above, but uses the raw script. | | **Linux/macOS Terminal** | `curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/speedtest-net/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py | python -` | Same output. | ### Quick command‑line test (if you have Python) If you’re comfortable running a one‑liner in a terminal, try this (works on Windows, macOS, Linux): ```bash curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/speedtest-net/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py | python - ``` It will automatically download the script, run it, and print something like: ``` Testing from Your ISP (Your City)... Retrieving speedtest.net configuration... Testing download speed........................................ Download: 85.23 Mbit/s Testing upload speed.......................................... Upload: 12.45 Mbit/s ``` ### What to look for - **Download speed** – how fast you can pull data (e.g., streaming, downloads). - **Upload speed** – how fast you can push data (e.g., video calls, uploads). - **Ping (latency)** – milliseconds to the test server; lower is better for gaming or real‑time apps. If you’d like me to run a command for you (e.g., the `curl | python` line) on a Windows machine, just let me know and I can execute it via the `cmd_controller_execute` tool. Otherwise, try one of the methods above and let me know what numbers you get!
